info.title: PKSE
info.author: Kiasta
info.details:
PKSE (Pokémon Save Editor) is a Pokémon save editor for Nintendo Switch consoles -- no PC or save transfers needed.

Supported games:
- FireRed/LeafGreen
- Let's Go, Pikachu!/Eevee!
- Sword/Shield
- Brilliant Diamond/Shining Pearl
- Legends: Arceus
- Scarlet/Violet
- Legends: Z-A

Features:
- Edit party and box Pokémon: species, level, IVs/EVs, nature, ability, moves, held item, ball, OT and met data, shininess and gender
- Trainer info and item pouches, with per-game item and count limits
- Pokémon creator -- build one from scratch in any supported game's format
- Legality checker flags illegal values as you edit; it never blocks or alters your data
- Cross-game bank: deposit from one game, withdraw into another, converted to the destination format with origin preserved
- HOME-style interface with full touch support
- On-console save backup and restore with retained history

Free, open source, built using PKHeX as a reference.

v1.2.2
PKSE Release 1.2.2 - Full Release Notes

 Version 1.2.2 Feature and Fix Release

This release adds a ribbon and mark editor, Hyper Training, Add All Items, an Alpha toggle- for the Legends games, and favorite folders- in the file browser. It also fixes about a hundred problems found by a full review of PKSE against PKHeX.

If you use the Pokémon Bank, update.- In Sword/Shield, Legends: Arceus, Scarlet/Violet and Legends: Z-A, moving a Pokémon in the Boxes view could copy it into every empty box slot. Several older games could refuse or damage a Pokémon withdrawn from the bank, and a Pokémon edited in a Generation 4–7 game could later disappear from the bank.

 New features

- Added a ribbon and mark editor. The Ribbons row on the details page now appears for every game that stores ribbons, Ruby/Sapphire/Emerald through Legends: Z-A, even when the Pokémon has none. Y- or a tap opens a Ribbons & Marks- grid with each ribbon's own image.
  - A- gives or removes the selected ribbon. L/R- change a Generation 3 contest rank or a Contest/Battle Memory count.
  - ZR- gives every ribbon and ZL- removes them all.
  - In Sword/Shield and later, X- affixes the selected ribbon.
  - Any ribbon can be given. As always, the legality checker reports and never refuses.
- Added Hyper Training.
  - The party card marks a Hyper Trained IV with HT, and the details page explains that marked IVs play at the maximum.
  - The stat editor has a Hyper Trained row in every game that has Hyper Training.
  - Setting it follows the games' rules: level 100 (50 in Scarlet/Violet and Legends: Z-A), an IV below the maximum, and, in Legends: Arceus, a Pokémon that has been through HOME. The row says why it refuses. Allow illegal values- lifts these limits.
- Added Add All Items. ZR- in the Items view adds an amount you choose (1–999) to every item every pouch can hold.
  - Each item stops at the most the game allows for that item, so HMs, TMs in Sword/Shield, Z-Rings and the like stay at their real limits.
  - A stack you already have is never lowered.
  - Key items are left out unless you switch them on, with a warning, because key items given early can skip or break story events.
- Added an Alpha toggle- for Legends: Arceus and Legends: Z-A. Turning Alpha on also gives the Pokémon the size a wild Alpha has. Turning it off leaves the size alone.
- Added favorite folders- to the file browser.
  - ZR- adds or removes the current folder, and favorites are marked with a star. ZL- lists them.
  - The browser also reopens in the folder you last picked a file from. Save files and imports each remember their own folder.
- A Pokémon withdrawn from the bank into another game now has you as its handling trainer, as Poké Transporter, Bank and HOME do. Before, it arrived with no handler. Pokémon already moved keep their old handler data until they are moved again.
- Glitch Pokémon in Red/Blue/Yellow and Gold/Silver/Crystal- (MissingNo., 'M and similar) are now kept. The storage view shows each as a locked ?- slot that still counts toward the box or party. Before, PKSE deleted them on load.

 Fixed - Pokémon cloned, lost or damaged

- Fixed an issue where moving a Pokémon in the Boxes view of Sword/Shield, Legends: Arceus, Scarlet/Violet or Legends: Z-A- could save a copy of it into every empty box slot.
- Fixed an issue where withdrawing a Pokémon from the bank after reopening it refused Diamond/Pearl, Platinum, Black/White and X/Y Pokémon, and put Ruby/Sapphire/Emerald and Sun/Moon Pokémon through a needless conversion that lost data. Pokémon moving between FireRed/LeafGreen and Ruby/Sapphire/Emerald now keep their data exactly.
- Fixed an issue where an edit in a Generation 4–7 game left the Pokémon's checksum stale. If that Pokémon was then deposited, the bank rejected it on the next load and erased it on the next save. Every edit on the details page now finishes the same way: stats, checksum, then the save marked as changed.
- Fixed an issue where HeartGold/SoulSilver could ignore edited boxes- the next time the game itself saved.
- Fixed an issue where Put Back- could drop a Pokémon in the wrong place.
  - Each Pokémon now goes back to where it came from, and a copy is simply dropped.
  - A Pokémon from another game is never placed in the save unconverted.
  - Anything with nowhere to go stays in your hand instead of being lost.
- Fixed an issue where a record PKSE couldn't read was deleted from the bank. It is now set aside and kept.
- Bad Eggs- are now written back untouched in every game, instead of being re-encoded.

 Fixed - saving and loading

- Fixed an issue where a damaged or cut-off Switch save- (Sword/Shield, Brilliant Diamond/Shining Pearl, Legends: Arceus, Scarlet/Violet, Legends: Z-A) could crash PKSE or be written back shorter than it was. It now fails to open with a message. A Switch FireRed/LeafGreen that has never been saved now says so, instead of opening an empty editor.
- Fixed an issue where editing the live game save overwrote PKSE's own pre-edit backup. That backup is now kept untouched, and your edits go to a copy named "… Edited".
- Fixed an issue where New backup- could make its folder from the game's display name instead of its title folder.
- Fixed an issue where a failed write could go unnoticed. A file you opened yourself is no longer overwritten if its backup copy failed.
- Fixed an issue where FireRed/LeafGreen- computed some save checksums over too little data.
- Fixed an issue where SoulSilver- could be identified as HeartGold, and where Generation 4 ignored the save's own language.
- Battle-team Pokémon- are now locked in the storage view in Sun/Moon, Sword/Shield, Brilliant Diamond/Shining Pearl, Scarlet/Violet and Legends: Z-A, as they are in the games.
- Fixed several bag and Pokédex details that drifted on save:
  - Brilliant Diamond/Shining Pearl's new-item order and "new" flags.
  - Legends: Z-A's new-item notification.
  - The Generation 5/6 berry pouch.
  - Scarlet/Violet's Pokédex display choice.
  - Sword/Shield's displayed gender and Alcremie.
  - The selected gender in Legends: Arceus.
  - Let's Go's size records.

 Fixed - Pokémon details and editing

- Fixed an issue where Shedinja- could get more than 1 HP in Generations 4–9.
- Fixed an issue where Docile- was treated as a stat-changing nature in Black/White and Black 2/White 2.
- Fixed an issue where the EXP field did nothing- in Ruby/Sapphire/Emerald and FireRed/LeafGreen, and where Red/Blue/Yellow updated only one of the two places it stores the level.
- Fixed an issue where Gold/Silver/Crystal names- were written without their end marker.
- Fixed an issue where Japanese Generation 3 trainer names- could be longer than the game allows, and Red/Blue/Yellow could write a cut-off name.
- Changing a Pokémon's ability, nature or shininess- now updates the related hidden values as the games and PKHeX require. This covers:
  - The PID ability bit and Black/White's hidden-ability flag.
  - Nature from the PID in Generations 5–6.
  - The encryption constant of a Pokémon from Generations 3–5.
  - The Wurmple evolution, and Black/White's PID/ID bit.
- Friendship now follows the current handler in X/Y through Ultra Sun/Ultra Moon.
- Obedience level now follows the met level in Scarlet/Violet and Legends: Z-A.
- Let's Go height and weight- now come out the same on every console, and are recomputed when the species or form changes.
- Fixed an issue where an emptied Scarlet/Violet move slot kept its PP.
- Fixed the shiny check for a trainer with ID 0.
- Gold/Silver/Crystal pickers and held items now use Gold/Silver/Crystal's own item list.
- Fixed several item limits:
  - Ruby/Sapphire/Emerald pouches stop at 99, and key items at 1.
  - Legends: Z-A's per-item limits apply in Edit Item.
  - Let's Go Mega Stones stop at 1.
- Fixed an issue where the EV limit of 252 per stat- was applied before Generation 6, which has no such limit.
- Sun/Moon now shows the six-digit trainer ID, and Red/Blue/Yellow and Gold/Silver/Crystal show their five-digit ID.

 Fixed - the creator

- A created Pokémon now gets its default nickname in its own language.
- In Generations 4–7 it gets a real met location.
- In Let's Go it gets a spirit, mood and received date.
- It starts with the game's own base friendship.

 Fixed - transfers and the bank

- Fixed an issue where moving a Pokémon between Sun/Moon/Ultra Sun/Ultra Moon and Sword/Shield or later lost its Generation 6/7 ribbons.
- A Generation 3 Pokémon moving to a newer game- now follows the real Pal Park path. It keeps its ribbons and markings, gets the transfer met location, and keeps shininess exactly as the games do. An un-nicknamed Pokémon gets its proper species name. An egg is hatched on the way. Moving it back into Generation 3 restores what it had.
- Fixed an issue where a held item was cleared- on a move into Sun/Moon or Ultra Sun/Ultra Moon.
- A Generation 1/2 Pokémon sent on through Poké Transporter- now gets its language from its species name, not from your console's language.
- Fixed an issue where a Sun/Moon trade evolution- wrote an X/Y-style memory.
- PKSM bank import now handles Scarlet/Violet Pokémon and a partly filled last box.

 Fixed - legality checker

- Fixed a Let's Go wild Pokémon one level above its spot's maximum- being reported as illegal. The catch combo raises a wild Pokémon's level by one.
- Moves are now checked against every game the Pokémon could have passed through, as PKHeX does. Smeargle's Sketch is recognised. ORAS Poké Flute and DexNav levels, Necrozma's fusion moves and Cosplay Pikachu are now handled.
- Fixed false warnings for:
  - Legends: Z-A's Latin-American Spanish language.
  - Brilliant Diamond/Shining Pearl traded eggs.
  - Scarlet/Violet unhatched eggs.
  - Blue-Striped Basculin with Reckless.
  - Platinum/HeartGold/SoulSilver's Faraway Place eggs.
- Real saves from Sun, Ultra Sun, Ultra Moon, Y, Alpha Sapphire, Shining Pearl and Let's Go Eevee now report far fewer false warnings, most of them none, with no new ones.
- Origin games now include FireRed/LeafGreen on Switch, with a Game Boy Advance origin mark, and Pokémon HOME's special values.

 Fixed - interface

- Fixed an issue where +- acted while a dialog was still open. In exit mode the control bar now says what A really does.
- Fixed an issue where dialogs dimmed their own button hints. The control bar now stays bright for whatever owns the input.
- Fixed an issue where the file browser opened in the wrong place on first use.
- Fixed Trade Evolve- when you chose not to evolve, the PKSM import cursor, and touch input on four dialogs.
- Form names now follow the game they are shown for.

 Notes

- The bank and the game save are saved separately, as before.
  - Leaving the bank with changes asks Save & Exit / Discard changes / Cancel- for the bank only, and the game save never writes the bank.
  - Discard- affects the bank only: a Pokémon you moved into the Box stays there until you save or discard the game.
  - Moving a Pokémon and then saving only one side can still copy or lose it, so save both.
- International Gold/Silver/Crystal text is read as English, as PKHeX does.
- For anyone building PKSE: a fresh checkout now also needs python tools/gen_ribbons.py for the ribbon images. The build stops and names the script if they are missing.

v1.2.1
PKSE Release 1.2.1 - Full Release Notes

 Version 1.2.1 Feature and Bug-Fix Release

This release adds standalone Pokémon file import and export, PKSE's own on-screen keyboard- and left-stick navigation, and fixes a long list of bugs. The most important are Legends: Arceus adding 1 to the "Number caught" research task of every Pokémon you own each time you saved, Let's Go halving  its Pokédex size records on every save, and Bank files that could be overwritten after a failed read.

If you have saved a Legends: Arceus game with an earlier version, please read the first section.- The extra research counts already in your save cannot be told apart from real ones, so they are not removed. They will not grow any further.

 New features

- Added Pokémon file import and export, thanks to @GlitchedZeus. Export any Pokémon from the Storage view's action menu, or import a .pk1–.pk9, .pb7, .pb8, .pa8 or .pa9 file into the Bank. PKHeX's encrypted files (.ek3–.ea9) import too. Export writes the plain form.
- Added PKSE's own on-screen keyboard. Every text and number prompt now opens a keyboard in the app's theme instead of the console's:
- Layouts:- letters, symbols (including ♂ ♀ … ×) and accented letters, switched with ZL/ZR. A number prompt gets a number pad, with a +/− key where a negative value is allowed.
- Buttons:- A types, B deletes, Y adds a space, X is Shift, L/R move the cursor, + accepts and − cancels.
- Touch and held buttons:- tap a key, or tap in the field to place the cursor. Holding a button repeats it.
- Length limit:- the field counts characters the way the games count them, and flashes when one does not fit.
- Japanese, Chinese and Korean:- the あ漢한 key opens the console's keyboard, as before.
- Added left-stick navigation, thanks to @GlitchedZeus. The left stick moves like the D-pad on every screen, with held repeat for long lists. Holding L/R now repeats on the save picker too.

 Fixed - Legends: Arceus

- Fixed an issue where every save added 1 to the "Number caught" research task of every Pokémon in your  party and boxes, edited or not. A legendary you can only catch once could show 6 after six Bank sessions. Now only a Pokémon that is new to the save is counted, and only once.
- A Pokémon new to the save now gets the same research credit the game gives a catch:
- Number caught.
- Number of alphas caught, if it is an alpha.
- The species' large, small, heavy or light task, if its size qualifies.
- Fixed an issue where a Pokémon withdrawn from the Bank into Legends: Arceus, or made in the creator, had a height and weight of 0. Both are now calculated the way the game calculates them.

 Fixed - Let's Go

- Fixed an issue where every save halved the Pokédex's smallest and largest height records. Records already halved by an earlier version are not repaired automatically.
- Fixed an issue where saving wrote the partner Pikachu or Eevee into the Pokédex size records, which the game does not do.
- Fixed an issue where saving an unedited game rewrote every empty box slot. Empty slots now keep the bytes the game wrote.

 Fixed - saves and the Bank

- Fixed an issue where a Bank file that exists but could not be read opened as an empty Bank, and the next Bank save overwrote it, losing every Pokémon it held. The file is now set aside with a message, and is never written over.
- Bank saves are now written to a temporary file first, so a save interrupted part-way can no longer leave
a damaged Bank.
- Fixed an issue where some save files PKHeX accepts were refused, including a VBA-M FireRed save and Japanese Gold/Silver/Crystal saves in 32 KiB files. PKSE now accepts exactly what PKHeX accepts.
- Fixed an issue where pressing A on a file PKSE refuses did nothing. The reason is now shown.
- Fixed an issue where some emulator save files did not open- because of their file size.
- Fixed an issue where a Gold/Silver/Crystal save padded to 128 KiB was read as a 64 KiB save. It is now read at its real size.
- Fixed an issue where saving an unedited Brilliant Diamond/Shining Pearl- game rewrote its empty box slots and the end of the trainer name. Both are now left exactly as the game wrote them.

 Fixed - Pokémon editing

- Fixed an issue where Make Shiny silently did nothing about 1 time in 11- on a Diamond/Pearl, Platinum, HeartGold/SoulSilver, Black/White or Black 2/White 2 Pokémon.
- Fixed an issue where Make Shiny in those games could give a Pokémon a PID that contradicts its stored gender. Shininess, gender, nature and the ability slot are now all kept.
- Fixed an issue where editing a Generation 4–7 Pokémon's IVs or EVs made a shiny Pokémon plain.
- Fixed an issue where discarding the only edit on the details page left "unsaved changes" showing.
- An egg in FireRed/LeafGreen or Ruby/Sapphire/Emerald now always keeps the game's egg name.

 Fixed - items

- Fixed an issue where an item Scarlet/Violet had never held, such as Sweet Herba Mystica, could not be added. It is now added with the flag the game sets when you first obtain an item.
- Add Item now says when it has left out an item because PKSE counts it as held.
- Fixed an issue where Scarlet/Violet and Legends: Z-A could mark items you have owned for weeks as new- (the red dot in the bag), or show them as favourites in PKSE.
- Fixed an issue where L/R did not change pouch in Generations 1, 2 and 4–7, so only the first pouch could be reached.
- Fixed an issue where an item added to a full pouch in Generations 1, 2 and 4–7 was shown and then dropped when you saved. Each pouch now has its real size and stack limit.

 Notes

- The automated tests are now part of the project.- A separate development build, PKSE-dev.nro, adds an on-console self test that writes only to scratch copies of your saves. Releases are the normal build, PKSE.nro, which does not include it.
- Developer documentation has been added: CLAUDE.md, a technical manual in docs/manual/, per-generation references in docs/integration/ and the coding standards in docs/CODING_STANDARDS.md. Contributors should read .github/CONTRIBUTING.md before opening a pull request.

v1.2.0
PKSE Release 1.2.0 - Full Release Notes

 Version 1.2.0 Feature Release

This release adds every Pokémon generation before the Switch. 26 titles from Red/Blue through Ultra
Sun/Ultra Moon, and fixes the non-English FireRed/LeafGreen releases never appearing on the save
picker. It also adds Trade Evolve, a third legality layer that asks whether a Pokémon could really
have been caught where it says it was, PKSM bank import, Tera Types, origin marks and search, and
fixes a long list of correctness bugs, including Legends: Arceus stats being wrong by roughly a
factor of three, and Japanese, Korean and Chinese text drawing as nothing.

An older game's save is a file, not an installed game.- Copy it onto your SD card, press Y — Open
Save File- on the save picker, and browse to it. Saves named main are listed too.

If you own FireRed/LeafGreen, your backup folders move on first launch.- They now carry the title ID,
so two releases of one game can no longer share one folder. An ambiguous folder is left alone and named
in the log, rather than guessed.

 New features

- Added 26 pre-Switch titles: Red/Blue/Yellow, Gold/Silver/Crystal, Ruby/Sapphire/Emerald, Diamond/Pearl/Platinum/HeartGold/SoulSilver, Black/White/Black 2/White 2, X/Y/Omega Ruby/Alpha Sapphire and Sun/Moon/Ultra Sun/Ultra Moon. Boxes, party, items, trainer details, the creator, the legality checker and the bank all work as they do on the Switch games, and each game reads its own- species data rather than a shared table.
- Added Trade Evolve- to the details page, for every Pokémon that evolves by trading in its own game, including the ones needing a held item, which is consumed if there is one but is not required. Clamperl asks which evolution you want. From X/Y onward a trade leaves a handling trainer behind, so those games ask whether to take one from a save you own or generate one.
- Added a third legality layer: whether a real encounter exists in the game a Pokémon claims to come from that could have produced it, across wild encounters, statics, gifts, trades, raids and Mystery Gift distributions. It covers all nineteen save formats and is informational only. PKSE never refuses an edit.
- Added PKSM bank import. Press −- in the Storage view to browse to a .bnk file, preview what it holds and commit it. All nine of PKSM's generation tags import.
- Added forward transfer for Generation 1 and 2 Pokémon- exactly as the Virtual Console games did. This is forward directional only, because a Generation 1 Pokémon has nowhere to record a nature, ability, PID or ball.
- Added name tables in nine languages, for every title, species, moves, abilities, natures, types, items, forms, locations and ribbons.
- Added the console's own fonts, so Japanese, Korean and Chinese names render in every game, for the names stored in the save as well as the ones PKSE supplies. They were being read correctly all along and drawn as nothing, because the bundled font has no CJK characters.
- Added Tera Types- for Scarlet/Violet, on the details page and as a badge under the Pokémon's types, Stellar included. Displayed, not editable.
- Added origin marks- to the Boxes and Storage views — the Kalos pentagon, the Alola clover, the Galar, Let's Go, BDSP, Legends: Arceus, Scarlet/Violet and Legends: Z-A marks, the Pokémon GO mark, and a Game Boy for a Virtual Console transfer. Generations 3 to 5 show a game name and no mark, because the games never had a stamp for one.
- Added search on Y- to every picker, the Items pouch and the file browser. Add Item has moved from Y to −- so that Y is search everywhere. The Box and Bank get Find- from the Storage menu (X), which highlights matches rather than hiding slots.
- Added the Egg Location picker, so egg sources like BDSP's "Nursery Couple" can be chosen rather than only displayed.
- Made Species editable. Changing it re-points what depends on it: form is clamped to one the new species has, gender is constrained to its ratio, the ability moves to the same slot, and experience is re-derived from the level. Moves are deliberately left alone.
- Added an "Auto-Legalize Unsupported Transfers"- setting, off by default. No game has ever let a Pokémon from another generation reach Generation 3, and with this on PKSE rebuilds such a Pokémon as a legal native of the game it is going to. It never lowers a level and never claims an event the Pokémon did not receive.
- The Handling Trainer row now appears for every format that has one, reading (none) when the Pokémon has never been traded, and says which of OT/HT is the active handler. Fields a format does not have are hidden rather than drawn as zero — a Generation 1 Pokémon has no Ability, Nature, Held Item or Ball row at all.

 Fixed - FireRed/LeafGreen not found

- Fixed an issue where FireRed/LeafGreen saves in any language but English reported "0 saves found". Those games ship one Switch title per language — no other Pokémon title does, so no other game was affected — and PKSE only knew the English pair, dropping every save whose title ID it did not recognise. All twelve are recognised now. This was about identifying the title, not about reading its language.
- Fixed an issue where two releases of one game shared a backup folder, so opening the French game could load the English save — and, with "write back to the game" on, write it into the French title. Nothing failed and nothing was logged, because the two saves are the same format.
- Fixed an issue where PKSE ignored a Pokémon save whose title ID it did not know, rather than identifying it by its contents.

 Fixed - saves being written incorrectly

Each of these was found by loading a real save, writing it straight back without editing anything, and
requiring the file to come back identical. None showed up as an error: the save was valid, it simply wrote
bytes PKSE had no business writing.

- Fixed an issue where empty Generation 3 party slots were stamped with "mail 0"- instead of the game's "no mail" marker.
- Fixed an issue where every Generation 3 party Pokémon's battle stats were recalculated on every save. The games refresh those only on level-up, evolution or a PC deposit, so a Pokémon trained since its last level-up legitimately stores lower stats than the formula gives. A Pokémon you actually edit still gets fresh stats.
- Fixed an issue where saving a Sword/Shield save moved items around inside the bag, even when no item had been edited. Nothing was ever lost, but the bag was no longer laid out the way the game left it.

 Fixed - eggs in a Generation 3 save

- Fixed an issue where an egg showed a garbled name and claimed to be Japanese. Generation 3 marks every egg, on every cartridge, by storing the Japanese word for egg as its nickname and setting its language to Japanese, and replaces both when it hatches. An egg now reads Egg, with (set when it hatches)- for its language.
- Fixed an issue where making a Pokémon an egg wrote an incomplete record- — the games write an internal flag, the placeholder name and the language together, and PKSE wrote only the flag.

 Fixed - stats, abilities and data tables

- Fixed an issue where every Legends: Arceus Pokémon's stats were wrong, by roughly a factor of three at low level. That game has Grit Values rather than EVs and scales the base stat directly. Boxed Pokémon were worst affected, since their stats are recalculated when the save loads.
- Fixed an issue where roughly thirty Pokémon had no base stats at all- and computed from a base of zero — Darmanitan, Aegislash, Wishiwashi, Minior, Eiscue, Morpeko, Thundurus, Landorus, Calyrex and Melmetal among them. Tauros was the Paldean Combat Breed in every game, including the ones that only have the Kanto one.
- Fixed an issue where abilities were checked against Scarlet/Violet's data in every game, reporting "Ability not legal for this species" for perfectly ordinary Pokémon — a Brilliant Diamond Piplup, or most of Legends: Arceus's Hisuian forms.
- Fixed an issue where an evolved Legends: Z-A Pokémon could be reported as holding an illegal ability. That game keeps the ability a Pokémon was caught with through evolution, so a Fletchling caught with Big Pecks is still a Big Pecks Fletchinder.
- Fixed an issue where Brilliant Diamond/Shining Pearl, Scarlet/Violet and Legends: Z-A could not be given a Hisui ball, and where a Legends: Arceus Pokémon moved into one of them had its ball replaced with a Poké Ball. Replacing it is Sword/Shield's rule alone.
- Fixed an issue where the TM pouch named item ids 420-427 "TM93" through "TM100". Those eight ids are HM01 through HM08.

 Fixed - transferring into a Generation 3 game

- Fixed an issue where a Pokémon moved into FireRed/LeafGreen was given a met location from the wrong region- — a transferred Generation 1 Pokémon arrived at "Abandoned Ship", which is in Hoenn. Generation 3 stores a met location in one byte in its own numbering, and the wider value was being copied straight across. Every transfer into Generation 3 was affected, not only the Generation 1 and 2 route this release adds. A Pokémon now lands somewhere the destination could actually have produced it; this does not make it legal, and is not meant to.
- Fixed an issue where a transferred Unown came out as a different letter. In Generation 3 the letter is part of the PID rather than a stored field, so regenerating the PID silently renamed it — and since each Tanoby chamber holds five letters, the renamed Unown also ended up somewhere its own letter never appears.
- A Generation 3 Pokémon returning to its own game- is unaffected and keeps its met location exactly. That is the one backward transfer that is genuinely legal.

 Fixed - names and interface

- Fixed an issue where ribbon names did not match the games: Battle Royale is Battle Royal Master, and Champion Battle, Champion Regional and Champion National are Battle Champion, Regional Champion- and National Champion. Two more carried disambiguation no game shows and are simply Champion- and Hoenn Champion.
- Fixed an issue where the reported DLC level was wrong for some Sword/Shield and Scarlet/Violet saves. Neither game records a DLC entitlement anywhere, so both now report their full content set. Nothing is gated on it.
- Fixed an issue where dialogs drew a second row of button hints- inside their own card. There is one control bar per screen, and it belongs to whatever owns the input.

 Notes

- Korean Generation 2 saves are deliberately not claimed.- They need a different character table and a differently shaped checksum, so PKSE refuses them rather than half-opening one.
- Red, Blue, Green, Gold, Silver, Diamond, Pearl, HeartGold, SoulSilver, Ruby and Sapphire cannot name themselves.- Each pair writes an identical save with no version byte, so PKSE names the pair.
- Gold, Silver and Crystal saves carrying a real-time clock footer are recognised, and Generation 3 Game Boy Advance saves keep theirs when written back, so berry growth and the tides are not reset.
- Before PKSE writes to a file you opened yourself, the original is copied to sdmc:/PKSE/FileBackups.
- Some form and ribbon names in languages other than English still use a shorter label- than the game does, where no verified source for the full wording was available. English is unaffected.
- Fetching assets for a fresh checkout is now four scripts rather than the Makefile: python tools/gen_fonts.py, gen_typeicons.py, gen_marks.py and gen_hdsprites.py. The build downloads nothing and stops with the script to run if one has not been.

Version 1.0 Release
This release brings several new features, title support, a whole new UI interface and a plethora of bug fixes.  

Newly supported titles:
- FireRed/LeafGreen
- Let's Go, Pikachu!/Eevee!
- Brilliant Diamond/Shining Pearl
- Legends: Arceus
- Scarlet/Violet

Editing:
- Party & box Pokémon: species, level, stats, IVs/EVs (AVs in Let's Go),
    nature, ability, moves, held item, ball, OT/met/origin, shininess and gender. Ribbons are still read-only.
- Trainer info and item pouches, with per-game item and count limits.
- Pokémon creator: build one from scratch in any game's format, with legal
    values highlighted.
- Legality checker: flags illegal values as you edit (informational; it never
    blocks or changes anything). Legality still a WIP.
- Cross-game bank: PKSE-native storage every supported game shares. A Pokémon
    deposited from one game is converted into the destination's format on
    withdrawal, preserving its origin (OT, IDs, met data, IVs, nature, PID).

Interface & save handling:
- HOME-style UI (NanoVG) with better 256px HD sprites, full touch controls, and
    scrollable storage and lists.
- On-console backup and restore, with retained backup history.
- Per-game save-version and DLC detection.
- On-screen error reporting (including when no backups are present).
